question: List all networks with their ID, name, tenant ID, status, MTU, administrative state, and VLAN transparency flag, ordered by tenant ID and network name.
SQL: SELECT id, name, tenant_id, status, mtu, admin_state_up, vlan_transparent FROM networks ORDER BY tenant_id, name, id;

question: Show the number of networks by status and administrative state, ordered from the largest count to the smallest.
SQL: SELECT status, admin_state_up, COUNT(*) AS network_count FROM networks GROUP BY status, admin_state_up ORDER BY network_count DESC;

question: For each tenant, show the number of networks, minimum MTU, maximum MTU, and average MTU. Include only tenants with at least two networks.
SQL: SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS network_count, MIN(mtu) AS min_mtu, MAX(mtu) AS max_mtu, AVG(mtu) AS avg_mtu FROM networks GROUP BY tenant_id HAVING COUNT(*) >= 2 ORDER BY network_count DESC;

question: List every port with its ID, network ID, MAC address, device owner, device ID, status, and administrative state, ordered by network ID and port ID.
SQL: SELECT id, network_id, mac_address, device_owner, device_id, status, admin_state_up FROM ports ORDER BY network_id, id;

question: Show the number of ports for each device owner and status combination.
SQL: SELECT device_owner, status, COUNT(*) AS port_count FROM ports GROUP BY device_owner, status ORDER BY port_count DESC;

question: List all subnets with their subnet name, network ID, CIDR, IP version, gateway IP, DHCP setting, and subnet pool ID.
SQL: SELECT id, name, network_id, cidr, ip_version, gateway_ip, enable_dhcp, subnetpool_id FROM subnets ORDER BY network_id, cidr;

question: For each IP version, count the number of subnets and how many of them have DHCP enabled.
SQL: SELECT ip_version, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count, SUM(CASE WHEN enable_dhcp = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dhcp_enabled_count FROM subnets GROUP BY ip_version ORDER BY ip_version;

question: List all routers with tenant ID, router ID, name, status, gateway port ID, SNAT setting, and administrative state.
SQL: SELECT tenant_id, id, name, status, gw_port_id, enable_snat, admin_state_up FROM routers ORDER BY tenant_id, name, id;

question: For each tenant, show the number of routers and how many routers have SNAT enabled.
SQL: SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS router_count, SUM(CASE WHEN enable_snat = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS snat_enabled_count FROM routers GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY router_count DESC;

question: Show the number of floating IPs by status and tenant.
SQL: SELECT tenant_id, status, COUNT(*) AS floating_ip_count FROM floatingips GROUP BY tenant_id, status ORDER BY tenant_id, floating_ip_count DESC;

question: List each security group with its ID, name, tenant ID, and standard attribute ID, ordered by tenant ID and name.
SQL: SELECT id, name, tenant_id, standard_attr_id FROM securitygroups ORDER BY tenant_id, name, id;

question: Show the count of security group rules by direction, ethertype, and protocol.
SQL: SELECT direction, ethertype, protocol, COUNT(*) AS rule_count FROM securitygrouprules GROUP BY direction, ethertype, protocol ORDER BY rule_count DESC;

question: For each network, show the network name, status, number of ports, and number of distinct device owners, including networks with no ports.
SQL: SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.name AS network_name, n.status, COUNT(p.id) AS port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT p.device_owner) AS distinct_device_owner_count FROM networks n LEFT JOIN ports p ON p.network_id = n.id GROUP BY n.id, n.name, n.status ORDER BY port_count DESC;

question: For each network, show the number of subnets, number of DHCP-enabled subnets, and number of distinct IP versions.
SQL: SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.name AS network_name, COUNT(s.id) AS subnet_count, SUM(CASE WHEN s.enable_dhcp = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS dhcp_enabled_subnet_count, COUNT(DISTINCT s.ip_version) AS ip_version_count FROM networks n LEFT JOIN subnets s ON s.network_id = n.id GROUP BY n.id, n.name ORDER BY subnet_count DESC;

question: List subnets with their network name, CIDR, gateway IP, first allocation pool IP, and last allocation pool IP.
SQL: SELECT s.id AS subnet_id, s.name AS subnet_name, n.name AS network_name, s.cidr, s.gateway_ip, p.first_ip, p.last_ip FROM subnets s JOIN networks n ON n.id = s.network_id LEFT JOIN ipallocationpools p ON p.subnet_id = s.id ORDER BY n.name, s.cidr;

question: For each subnet, show the CIDR, number of allocated IP addresses, number of DNS nameservers, and number of host routes.
SQL: SELECT s.id AS subnet_id, s.cidr, COUNT(DISTINCT ia.ip_address) AS allocated_ip_count, COUNT(DISTINCT dns.address) AS dns_nameserver_count, COUNT(DISTINCT sr.destination) AS host_route_count FROM subnets s LEFT JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.subnet_id = s.id LEFT JOIN dnsnameservers dns ON dns.subnet_id = s.id LEFT JOIN subnetroutes sr ON sr.subnet_id = s.id GROUP BY s.id, s.cidr ORDER BY allocated_ip_count DESC;

question: For each port, show the port name, network name, MAC address, number of allocated IPs, and whether port security is enabled.
SQL: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.name AS port_name, n.name AS network_name, p.mac_address, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS allocated_ip_count, ps.port_security_enabled FROM ports p JOIN networks n ON n.id = p.network_id LEFT JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN portsecuritybindings ps ON ps.port_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name, n.name, p.mac_address, ps.port_security_enabled ORDER BY allocated_ip_count DESC;

question: Find ports with more than one allocated IP address and show the port, network, device owner, and allocated IP count.
SQL: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.name AS port_name, n.name AS network_name, p.device_owner, COUNT(ia.ip_address) AS allocated_ip_count FROM ports p JOIN networks n ON n.id = p.network_id JOIN ipallocations ia ON ia.port_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name, n.name, p.device_owner HAVING COUNT(ia.ip_address) > 1 ORDER BY allocated_ip_count DESC;

question: For each router, show its name, status, gateway port status, gateway network name, and SNAT setting, including routers without a gateway port.
SQL: SELECT r.id AS router_id, r.name AS router_name, r.status AS router_status, p.status AS gateway_port_status, n.name AS gateway_network_name, r.enable_snat FROM routers r LEFT JOIN ports p ON p.id = r.gw_port_id LEFT JOIN networks n ON n.id = p.network_id ORDER BY r.tenant_id, r.name;

question: For each router and router port type, show attached port count and number of distinct networks reached through those ports.
SQL: SELECT r.id AS router_id, r.name AS router_name, rp.port_type, COUNT(rp.port_id) AS attached_port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT p.network_id) AS distinct_network_count FROM routers r JOIN routerports rp ON rp.router_id = r.id JOIN ports p ON p.id = rp.port_id GROUP BY r.id, r.name, rp.port_type ORDER BY attached_port_count DESC;

question: For each router, show attached port count, floating IP count, and distinct fixed port count used by floating IPs.
SQL: SELECT r.id AS router_id, r.name AS router_name, COUNT(DISTINCT rp.port_id) AS attached_port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) AS floating_ip_count, COUNT(DISTINCT f.fixed_port_id) AS floating_fixed_port_count FROM routers r LEFT JOIN routerports rp ON rp.router_id = r.id LEFT JOIN floatingips f ON f.router_id = r.id GROUP BY r.id, r.name ORDER BY floating_ip_count DESC, attached_port_count DESC;

question: List floating IPs with floating network name, fixed port name, fixed IP address, router name, and status.
SQL: SELECT f.id AS floating_ip_id, f.floating_ip_address, fn.name AS floating_network_name, fp.name AS fixed_port_name, f.fixed_ip_address, r.name AS router_name, f.status FROM floatingips f LEFT JOIN networks fn ON fn.id = f.floating_network_id LEFT JOIN ports fp ON fp.id = f.fixed_port_id LEFT JOIN routers r ON r.id = f.router_id ORDER BY f.status, f.floating_ip_address;

question: For each security group, show rule count, ingress rule count, egress rule count, and number of ports bound to the group.
SQL: SELECT sg.id AS security_group_id, sg.name AS security_group_name, sg.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT sgr.id) AS rule_count, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN sgr.direction = 'ingress' THEN sgr.id END) AS ingress_rule_count, COUNT(DISTINCT CASE WHEN sgr.direction = 'egress' THEN sgr.id END) AS egress_rule_count, COUNT(DISTINCT sgb.port_id) AS bound_port_count FROM securitygroups sg LEFT JOIN securitygrouprules sgr ON sgr.security_group_id = sg.id LEFT JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgb ON sgb.security_group_id = sg.id GROUP BY sg.id, sg.name, sg.tenant_id ORDER BY rule_count DESC;

question: Find ports assigned to more than one security group and show their network, device owner, and security group count.
SQL: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.name AS port_name, n.name AS network_name, p.device_owner, COUNT(sgb.security_group_id) AS security_group_count FROM ports p JOIN networks n ON n.id = p.network_id JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgb ON sgb.port_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name, n.name, p.device_owner HAVING COUNT(sgb.security_group_id) > 1 ORDER BY security_group_count DESC;

question: For each network, show total security group assignments across its ports and the number of distinct security groups used.
SQL: SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.name AS network_name, COUNT(sgb.security_group_id) AS security_group_assignment_count, COUNT(DISTINCT sgb.security_group_id) AS distinct_security_group_count FROM networks n LEFT JOIN ports p ON p.network_id = n.id LEFT JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgb ON sgb.port_id = p.id GROUP BY n.id, n.name ORDER BY security_group_assignment_count DESC;

question: For each ML2 network type and physical network, show the number of network segments and number of distinct networks.
SQL: SELECT network_type, physical_network, COUNT(*) AS segment_count, COUNT(DISTINCT network_id) AS distinct_network_count FROM ml2_network_segments GROUP BY network_type, physical_network ORDER BY segment_count DESC;

question: For each network, show its ML2 network type, physical network, segmentation ID, and whether the network is external.
SQL: SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.name AS network_name, seg.network_type, seg.physical_network, seg.segmentation_id, ex.is_default AS is_default_external_network FROM networks n LEFT JOIN ml2_network_segments seg ON seg.network_id = n.id LEFT JOIN externalnetworks ex ON ex.network_id = n.id ORDER BY n.name, seg.segment_index;

question: For each host and VIF type, show the number of bound ports and the number of distinct networks those ports belong to.
SQL: SELECT b.host, b.vif_type, COUNT(*) AS bound_port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT p.network_id) AS distinct_network_count FROM ml2_port_bindings b JOIN ports p ON p.id = b.port_id GROUP BY b.host, b.vif_type ORDER BY bound_port_count DESC;

question: For each DHCP agent host, show the number of bound networks and the number of distinct tenants owning those networks.
SQL: SELECT a.host, COUNT(DISTINCT nb.network_id) AS bound_network_count, COUNT(DISTINCT n.tenant_id) AS distinct_tenant_count FROM networkdhcpagentbindings nb JOIN agents a ON a.id = nb.dhcp_agent_id JOIN networks n ON n.id = nb.network_id GROUP BY a.host ORDER BY bound_network_count DESC;

question: For each tenant, show network count, port count, subnet count, router count, and floating IP count in one row.
SQL: WITH tenant_networks AS (SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS network_count FROM networks GROUP BY tenant_id), tenant_ports AS (SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS port_count FROM ports GROUP BY tenant_id), tenant_subnets AS (SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS subnet_count FROM subnets GROUP BY tenant_id), tenant_routers AS (SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS router_count FROM routers GROUP BY tenant_id), tenant_fips AS (SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(*) AS floating_ip_count FROM floatingips GROUP BY tenant_id) SELECT tn.tenant_id, tn.network_count, COALESCE(tp.port_count, 0) AS port_count, COALESCE(ts.subnet_count, 0) AS subnet_count, COALESCE(tr.router_count, 0) AS router_count, COALESCE(tf.floating_ip_count, 0) AS floating_ip_count FROM tenant_networks tn LEFT JOIN tenant_ports tp ON tp.tenant_id = tn.tenant_id LEFT JOIN tenant_subnets ts ON ts.tenant_id = tn.tenant_id LEFT JOIN tenant_routers tr ON tr.tenant_id = tn.tenant_id LEFT JOIN tenant_fips tf ON tf.tenant_id = tn.tenant_id ORDER BY tn.network_count DESC;

question: Rank networks within each tenant by port count and return the top three networks for every tenant.
SQL: WITH network_port_counts AS (SELECT n.tenant_id, n.id AS network_id, n.name AS network_name, COUNT(p.id) AS port_count FROM networks n LEFT JOIN ports p ON p.network_id = n.id GROUP BY n.tenant_id, n.id, n.name), ranked AS (SELECT network_port_counts.*, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY tenant_id ORDER BY port_count DESC, network_id) AS tenant_network_rank FROM network_port_counts) SELECT tenant_id, network_id, network_name, port_count, tenant_network_rank FROM ranked WHERE tenant_network_rank <= 3 ORDER BY tenant_id, tenant_network_rank;

question: Find networks whose port count is above the average port count across all networks. Show the network, tenant, port count, and average port count.
SQL: WITH network_port_counts AS (SELECT n.tenant_id, n.id AS network_id, n.name AS network_name, COUNT(p.id) AS port_count FROM networks n LEFT JOIN ports p ON p.network_id = n.id GROUP BY n.tenant_id, n.id, n.name), avg_counts AS (SELECT AVG(port_count) AS avg_port_count FROM network_port_counts) SELECT npc.tenant_id, npc.network_id, npc.network_name, npc.port_count, ac.avg_port_count FROM network_port_counts npc CROSS JOIN avg_counts ac WHERE npc.port_count > ac.avg_port_count ORDER BY npc.port_count DESC;

question: For each tenant, calculate quota usage percentage for every resource where a positive quota limit exists.
SQL: SELECT q.tenant_id, q.resource, q.`limit`, u.in_use, u.reserved, 100 * (COALESCE(u.in_use, 0) + COALESCE(u.reserved, 0)) / NULLIF(q.`limit`, 0) AS quota_usage_percent FROM quotas q LEFT JOIN quotausages u ON u.tenant_id = q.tenant_id AND u.resource = q.resource WHERE q.`limit` > 0 ORDER BY quota_usage_percent DESC;

question: For each tenant, show the number of quota resources, total in-use quota units, and total reserved quota units.
SQL: SELECT tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT resource) AS quota_resource_count, SUM(in_use) AS total_in_use, SUM(reserved) AS total_reserved FROM quotausages GROUP BY tenant_id ORDER BY total_in_use DESC;

question: For each QoS policy, show policy name, tenant, number of bandwidth limit rules, maximum Kbps, and number of networks bound to the policy.
SQL: SELECT qp.id AS qos_policy_id, qp.name AS qos_policy_name, qp.tenant_id, COUNT(DISTINCT br.id) AS bandwidth_rule_count, MAX(br.max_kbps) AS max_kbps, COUNT(DISTINCT npb.network_id) AS bound_network_count FROM qos_policies qp LEFT JOIN qos_bandwidth_limit_rules br ON br.qos_policy_id = qp.id LEFT JOIN qos_network_policy_bindings npb ON npb.policy_id = qp.id GROUP BY qp.id, qp.name, qp.tenant_id ORDER BY bound_network_count DESC, max_kbps DESC;

question: For each QoS policy, show how many networks and how many ports are directly bound to it.
SQL: SELECT qp.id AS qos_policy_id, qp.name AS qos_policy_name, COUNT(DISTINCT npb.network_id) AS network_binding_count, COUNT(DISTINCT ppb.port_id) AS port_binding_count FROM qos_policies qp LEFT JOIN qos_network_policy_bindings npb ON npb.policy_id = qp.id LEFT JOIN qos_port_policy_bindings ppb ON ppb.policy_id = qp.id GROUP BY qp.id, qp.name ORDER BY network_binding_count DESC, port_binding_count DESC;

question: For each load balancer, show listener count, pool count, member count, bytes in, bytes out, and active connections.
SQL: SELECT lb.id AS loadbalancer_id, lb.name AS loadbalancer_name, lb.vip_address, COUNT(DISTINCT l.id) AS listener_count, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS pool_count, COUNT(DISTINCT m.id) AS member_count, stats.bytes_in, stats.bytes_out, stats.active_connections FROM lbaas_loadbalancers lb LEFT JOIN lbaas_listeners l ON l.loadbalancer_id = lb.id LEFT JOIN lbaas_pools p ON p.loadbalancer_id = lb.id LEFT JOIN lbaas_members m ON m.pool_id = p.id LEFT JOIN lbaas_loadbalancer_statistics stats ON stats.loadbalancer_id = lb.id GROUP BY lb.id, lb.name, lb.vip_address, stats.bytes_in, stats.bytes_out, stats.active_connections ORDER BY member_count DESC;

question: For each LBaaS pool, show protocol, load-balancing algorithm, health monitor type, member count, and average member weight.
SQL: SELECT p.id AS pool_id, p.name AS pool_name, p.protocol, p.lb_algorithm, hm.type AS healthmonitor_type, COUNT(m.id) AS member_count, AVG(m.weight) AS avg_member_weight FROM lbaas_pools p LEFT JOIN lbaas_healthmonitors hm ON hm.id = p.healthmonitor_id LEFT JOIN lbaas_members m ON m.pool_id = p.id GROUP BY p.id, p.name, p.protocol, p.lb_algorithm, hm.type ORDER BY member_count DESC;

question: For each load balancer protocol, show listener count, average connection limit, and number of distinct default pools.
SQL: SELECT protocol, COUNT(*) AS listener_count, AVG(connection_limit) AS avg_connection_limit, COUNT(DISTINCT default_pool_id) AS distinct_default_pool_count FROM lbaas_listeners GROUP BY protocol ORDER BY listener_count DESC;

question: For each VPN service, show router name, subnet CIDR, number of IPsec site connections, and number of distinct peer addresses.
SQL: SELECT v.id AS vpnservice_id, v.name AS vpnservice_name, r.name AS router_name, s.cidr AS subnet_cidr, COUNT(c.id) AS connection_count, COUNT(DISTINCT c.peer_address) AS distinct_peer_address_count FROM vpnservices v LEFT JOIN routers r ON r.id = v.router_id LEFT JOIN subnets s ON s.id = v.subnet_id LEFT JOIN ipsec_site_connections c ON c.vpnservice_id = v.id GROUP BY v.id, v.name, r.name, s.cidr ORDER BY connection_count DESC;

question: For each IPsec connection, show VPN service name, IKE policy name, IPsec policy name, peer address, MTU, status, and administrative state.
SQL: SELECT c.id AS connection_id, c.name AS connection_name, v.name AS vpnservice_name, ike.name AS ike_policy_name, ipsec.name AS ipsec_policy_name, c.peer_address, c.mtu, c.status, c.admin_state_up FROM ipsec_site_connections c LEFT JOIN vpnservices v ON v.id = c.vpnservice_id LEFT JOIN ikepolicies ike ON ike.id = c.ikepolicy_id LEFT JOIN ipsecpolicies ipsec ON ipsec.id = c.ipsecpolicy_id ORDER BY c.status, c.name;

question: For each IKE version and encryption algorithm, show the number of IKE policies and average lifetime value.
SQL: SELECT ike_version, encryption_algorithm, COUNT(*) AS policy_count, AVG(lifetime_value) AS avg_lifetime_value FROM ikepolicies GROUP BY ike_version, encryption_algorithm ORDER BY policy_count DESC;

question: For each firewall policy, show firewall count, firewall rule count, shared flag, and audited flag.
SQL: SELECT fp.id AS firewall_policy_id, fp.name AS firewall_policy_name, fp.shared, fp.audited, COUNT(DISTINCT fw.id) AS firewall_count, COUNT(DISTINCT fr.id) AS firewall_rule_count FROM firewall_policies fp LEFT JOIN firewalls fw ON fw.firewall_policy_id = fp.id LEFT JOIN firewall_rules fr ON fr.firewall_policy_id = fp.id GROUP BY fp.id, fp.name, fp.shared, fp.audited ORDER BY firewall_rule_count DESC;

question: For each firewall rule protocol and action, show rule count and the number of enabled rules.
SQL: SELECT protocol, action, COUNT(*) AS rule_count, SUM(CASE WHEN enabled = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS enabled_rule_count FROM firewall_rules GROUP BY protocol, action ORDER BY rule_count DESC;

question: For each metering label, show rule count, excluded rule count, and number of distinct remote IP prefixes.
SQL: SELECT ml.id AS metering_label_id, ml.name AS metering_label_name, COUNT(mlr.id) AS rule_count, SUM(CASE WHEN mlr.excluded = 1 THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS excluded_rule_count, COUNT(DISTINCT mlr.remote_ip_prefix) AS distinct_remote_prefix_count FROM meteringlabels ml LEFT JOIN meteringlabelrules mlr ON mlr.metering_label_id = ml.id GROUP BY ml.id, ml.name ORDER BY rule_count DESC;

question: For each address scope, show IP version, shared flag, number of subnet pools, and number of distinct tenants using those subnet pools.
SQL: SELECT a.id AS address_scope_id, a.name AS address_scope_name, a.ip_version, a.shared, COUNT(sp.id) AS subnetpool_count, COUNT(DISTINCT sp.tenant_id) AS subnetpool_tenant_count FROM address_scopes a LEFT JOIN subnetpools sp ON sp.address_scope_id = a.id GROUP BY a.id, a.name, a.ip_version, a.shared ORDER BY subnetpool_count DESC;

question: For each subnet pool, show pool name, IP version, prefix length range, number of prefixes, and number of subnets using the pool.
SQL: SELECT sp.id AS subnetpool_id, sp.name AS subnetpool_name, sp.ip_version, sp.min_prefixlen, sp.default_prefixlen, sp.max_prefixlen, COUNT(DISTINCT spp.cidr) AS prefix_count, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS subnet_count FROM subnetpools sp LEFT JOIN subnetpoolprefixes spp ON spp.subnetpool_id = sp.id LEFT JOIN subnets s ON s.subnetpool_id = sp.id GROUP BY sp.id, sp.name, sp.ip_version, sp.min_prefixlen, sp.default_prefixlen, sp.max_prefixlen ORDER BY subnet_count DESC;

question: For each tenant, show total allowed address pairs and the number of distinct ports with allowed address pairs.
SQL: SELECT p.tenant_id, COUNT(aap.ip_address) AS allowed_address_pair_count, COUNT(DISTINCT aap.port_id) AS port_count_with_allowed_pairs FROM allowedaddresspairs aap JOIN ports p ON p.id = aap.port_id GROUP BY p.tenant_id ORDER BY allowed_address_pair_count DESC;

question: Find ports whose port security is disabled but that still have security group bindings. Show the port, network, tenant, and security group count.
SQL: SELECT p.id AS port_id, p.name AS port_name, n.name AS network_name, p.tenant_id, ps.port_security_enabled, COUNT(sgb.security_group_id) AS security_group_count FROM ports p JOIN networks n ON n.id = p.network_id JOIN portsecuritybindings ps ON ps.port_id = p.id LEFT JOIN securitygroupportbindings sgb ON sgb.port_id = p.id WHERE ps.port_security_enabled = 0 GROUP BY p.id, p.name, n.name, p.tenant_id, ps.port_security_enabled HAVING COUNT(sgb.security_group_id) > 0 ORDER BY security_group_count DESC;

question: For each network, show port count, subnet count, floating IP count on that network, and whether it is marked as an external network.
SQL: SELECT n.id AS network_id, n.name AS network_name, COUNT(DISTINCT p.id) AS port_count, COUNT(DISTINCT s.id) AS subnet_count, COUNT(DISTINCT f.id) AS floating_ip_count, CASE WHEN ex.network_id IS NULL THEN 0 ELSE 1 END AS is_external_network FROM networks n LEFT JOIN ports p ON p.network_id = n.id LEFT JOIN subnets s ON s.network_id = n.id LEFT JOIN floatingips f ON f.floating_network_id = n.id LEFT JOIN externalnetworks ex ON ex.network_id = n.id GROUP BY n.id, n.name, ex.network_id ORDER BY floating_ip_count DESC, port_count DESC;
